whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. That means your claim isn't artificially limited by a state-imposed maximum.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we win or settle your case. This lets injured people pursue a claim without worrying about hourly rates or retainers.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your claim involves a government agency, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's wise not to wait.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility. Your total compensation would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't barred entirely.

items.question: Where do injury collisions tend to cluster in Stanton?
items.answer: Public-record data shows crashes reported along corridors like Beach Boulevard, Katella Avenue, Cerritos Avenue, and Route 39, with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.
